mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-01.title: Proportion
mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-01.body:
$\frac{10 \text{ in}}{25 \text{ min}} = \frac{18.7 \text{ in}}{M}$, so $10M = 467.5$ and $M = 46.75 \approx 47$ minutes.

**Answer: 47 minutes**

mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-01.title: Minutes per inch
mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-01.body:
$25 \div 10 = 2.5$ minutes per inch (and $60 \div 24 = 2.5$ too). Then $18.7 \times 2.5 = 46.75 \approx 47$ minutes.

**Answer: 47 minutes**

mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-02.title: Compute in inch-feet, then convert
mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-02.body:
$48{,}000{,}000 \times 34.2 = 1{,}641{,}600{,}000$ (square feet × inches). Dividing by 12 inches per foot gives $136{,}800{,}000$ cubic feet.

**Answer: 136,800,000 cubic feet**

mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-03.title: Tons per cubic foot
mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-03.body:
One cubic foot weighs $15 \div 2000 = 0.0075$ ton, so the snow weighs $136{,}800{,}000 \times 0.0075 = 1{,}026{,}000$ tons.

**Answer: 1,026,000 tons**

mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-04.title: Add the rates
mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-04.body:
Per minute, Kenny does $\frac1{22}$ of the job and Isaiah $\frac1{14}$. Together: $\frac1{22} + \frac1{14} = \frac{7 + 11}{154} = \frac{18}{154} = \frac{9}{77}$ of the job per minute. Time $= \frac{77}{9} \approx 8.56 \approx 8.6$ minutes.

**Answer: 8.6 minutes**

mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-04.title: Harmonic formula
mathcounts-potw-2025-12-08-04.body:
For two workers taking $a$ and $b$ minutes, together they take $\frac{ab}{a+b} = \frac{22 \times 14}{36} = \frac{308}{36} \approx 8.56$ minutes, which is 8.6 to the nearest tenth.

**Answer: 8.6 minutes**
